lemmas.proof_markdown:
Put $\delta=\operatorname{wdeg}B$. Then $\deg_ZB\le\lfloor\delta/d\rfloor<p$. Suppose an irreducible polynomial $C$ divides both $B$ and $B_Z$. Writing $B=CE$, squarefreeness gives $C\nmid E$, while differentiation modulo $C$ gives $C\mid C_ZE$. Hence $C\mid C_Z$, so $C_Z=0$. In characteristic $p$, every positive $Z$-exponent of $C$ is therefore divisible by $p$. Since $\deg_ZC<p$, the polynomial $C$ is independent of $Z$, contradicting the primitivity of $B$. Thus $\gcd(B,B_Z)=1$.

The strict threshold is sharp: $Z^p-X$ is primitive, squarefree, smooth, and absolutely irreducible, has weighted degree $dp$, and has zero $Z$-derivative.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Let $p$ be prime and let $101\le d<p$. Give $X,Y,Z$ weights $(1,1,d)$. If $B\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]$ is squarefree, primitive as a polynomial in $Z$, and satisfies $\operatorname{wdeg}B<dp$, then $\gcd(B,B_Z)=1$.
lemmas.title: Vertical separability

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Write $U=\sum_iU_iZ^i$ and $V=\sum_jV_jZ^j$. The weighted-degree constraints give $\deg U_i\le u-di$ and $\deg V_j\le v-dj$. The nonzero resultant $R=\operatorname{Res}_Z(U,V)$ is homogeneous of degree $s$ in the coefficients of $U$ and degree $r$ in those of $V$. Every resultant monomial has total vertical-index weight $rs$, so its ordinary $(X,Y)$-degree is at most $su+rv-drs$. Hence $\deg R\le su+rv-drs$.

For each $L\in\mathcal T$, the specialized polynomials $U(L(t),Z)$ and $V(L(t),Z)$ have the common factor $Z-P_L(t)$, so $R(L(t))\equiv0$. The affine linear equation of $L$ therefore divides $R$. Distinct lines give distinct factors, proving the bound. No leading coefficient is divided out.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Let $p$ be prime and let $101\le d<p$, with weights $\operatorname{wt}(X)=\operatorname{wt}(Y)=1$ and $\operatorname{wt}(Z)=d$. Let $U,V\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]$ be nonzero and coprime, with $u=\operatorname{wdeg}U$, $v=\operatorname{wdeg}V$, $r=\deg_ZU$, and $s=\deg_ZV$. Let $\mathcal T$ be a family of distinct affine lines with parametrizations $L(t)$ and labels $P_L\in\mathbb F_p[t]$ of degree at most $d$ such that $U(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv V(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0$ for every $L\in\mathcal T$. Then $|\mathcal T|\le su+rv-drs$.
lemmas.title: Weighted resultant bound

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Frobenius acts transitively on the $k$ absolute factors of $C$. It preserves weighted and vertical degrees, so every factor has weighted degree $\delta/k$ and vertical degree $r/k$. Since the product of their graph restrictions vanishes in the domain $\overline{\mathbb F}_p[t]$, at least one factor vanishes on each graph. Applying Frobenius to that identity shows that every conjugate vanishes there.

Two distinct conjugates are coprime. Applying [P2] after extending scalars to $\overline{\mathbb F}_p$ gives $|\mathcal T|\le 2(r/k)(\delta/k)-d(r/k)^2=(2r\delta-dr^2)/k^2$. Finally, $\delta^2/d-(2r\delta-dr^2)=(\delta-dr)^2/d\ge0$. Since $k\ge2$, the last two bounds follow.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Let $p$ be prime and let $101\le d<p$, with weights $(1,1,d)$. Let $C\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]$ be irreducible and $Z$-dependent, with $\delta=\operatorname{wdeg}C$, $r=\deg_ZC$, and exactly $k\ge2$ absolute factors. If $\mathcal T$ is a family of distinct affine $\mathbb F_p$-lines with degree-at-most-$d$ labels $P_L$ satisfying $C(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0$, then $|\mathcal T|\le(2r\delta-dr^2)/k^2\le\delta^2/(dk^2)\le\delta^2/(4d)$.
lemmas.title: Frobenius purification

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Primitivity excludes base-only irreducible factors. Assign each line in $\mathcal T$ to one geometrically reducible factor supporting it. If the distinct assigned factors have weighted degrees $\delta_i$, then [P3] gives at most $\delta_i^2/(4d)$ assigned lines for the $i$th factor. Therefore $|\mathcal T|\le\sum_i\delta_i^2/(4d)\le(\sum_i\delta_i)^2/(4d)\le D^2/(4d)$. This is the sole union loss.

For sharpness, $C$ has vertical degree $2$ and weighted degree $2d$. It is irreducible over $\mathbb F_p$: a factorization would make $
u H_0^2$ a square in $\mathbb F_p(X,Y)$ and hence make $
u$ a square. Over $\overline{\mathbb F}_p$, it splits into $Z-\sqrt
u H_0$ and $Z+\sqrt
u H_0$. Each of the $d$ base lines dividing $H_0$, with label zero, is a graph line. On any other line, a graph label $q_L$ would give $(q_L/H_0(L))^2=
u$ in $\mathbb F_p(t)$, which is impossible. Thus exactly $d$ graph lines occur.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Let $p$ be prime and let $101\le d<p$, with weights $(1,1,d)$. Let $B\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]$ be primitive in $Z$ and satisfy $\operatorname{wdeg}B\le D$. Let $\mathcal T$ be a family of distinct affine $\mathbb F_p$-lines with degree-at-most-$d$ labels such that every $L\in\mathcal T$ is supported by an $\mathbb F_p$-irreducible, geometrically reducible factor of $B$. Then $|\mathcal T|\le D^2/(4d)$. If additionally $p>2d$, $\nu\in\mathbb F_p^\times$ is a nonsquare, and $H_0$ is a product of $d$ distinct affine-line equations, then $C=Z^2-\nu H_0^2$ is $\mathbb F_p$-irreducible with two absolute factors and supports exactly $d=(2d)^2/(4d)$ degree-at-most-$d$ graph lines.
lemmas.title: Factor aggregation

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Fix $(L,\tau)\in\mathcal E$, write $w=(L(\tau),f(L(\tau)))$, and let $v_L=(v_{L,1},v_{L,2})$ be the direction of $L$. Differentiating the formal graph identity gives $B_X(w)v_{L,1}+B_Y(w)v_{L,2}+B_Z(w)P_L'(\tau)=0$. Ramification gives $B_Z(w)=0$, while smoothness gives $(B_X(w),B_Y(w))\ne(0,0)$. Thus $v_L$ lies in the unique projective kernel direction of the nonzero functional $(B_X(w),B_Y(w))$.

All accepted incidences above a fixed base point have the same lift $(x,f(x))$. Hence that point permits at most one affine graph line. Summing over the $p^2$ base points gives $|\mathcal E|\le p^2$. Division by the ambient $p^2(p+1)$ incidences gives the normalized bound. No derivative is divided by.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Let $p$ be prime and let $101\le d<p$. Let $B\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]$, let $f:\mathbb F_p^2\to\mathbb F_p$, and let $\mathcal T$ be a family of affine lines parametrized by $L(t)$ with labels $P_L\in\mathbb F_p[t]$ of degree at most $d$ satisfying $B(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0$. Let $\mathcal E$ be the set of pairs $(L,\tau)$ satisfying $P_L(\tau)=f(L(\tau))$ and $B_Z(L(\tau),P_L(\tau))=0$. If every lift $(L(\tau),P_L(\tau))$ belonging to $\mathcal E$ is smooth on $B=0$, then $|\mathcal E|\le p^2$, and $|\mathcal E|/[p^2(p+1)]\le1/(p+1)$.
lemmas.title: Smooth ramification sparsity

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Since $D<2d$ and $B$ is $Z$-dependent, $B=a(X,Y)Z+b(X,Y)$ with $\deg a\le D-d$ and $\deg b\le D$. Primitivity gives $\gcd(a,b)=1$, and Gauss's lemma makes this primitive linear polynomial absolutely irreducible.

Because $B_Z=a$, a base point admits a ramified lift exactly when $a=b=0$. Bézout's theorem therefore bounds the ramified base set by $\deg a\deg b\le D(D-d)$. Deleting all these base vertices removes normalized incidence mass at most $D(D-d)/p^2$.

If a graph line were identically ramified, then $a(L(t))\equiv0$; substituting into $B(L(t),P(t))\equiv0$ gives $b(L(t))\equiv0$. The line equation would divide both $a$ and $b$, contradicting their coprimality.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Let $p$ be prime, let $101\le d<p$, and let $d\le D<2d$. Give $X,Y,Z$ weights $(1,1,d)$. Let $B\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]$ be primitive in $Z$, $Z$-dependent, and satisfy $\operatorname{wdeg}B\le D$. Then $|\{(x,y)\in\mathbb F_p^2:\exists z\in\mathbb F_p,\ B(x,y,z)=B_Z(x,y,z)=0\}|\le D(D-d)$, and there is no affine-line parametrization $L(t)$ with a degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial $P(t)$ satisfying both $B(L(t),P(t))\equiv0$ and $B_Z(L(t),P(t))\equiv0$.
lemmas.title: Linear vertical regime

lemmas.proof_markdown:
The definitions give $\deg H=2s+e=d+1=D$, so $\operatorname{wdeg}B=D<p$. The coefficients $X$ and $H(Y)$ are coprime. Thus $B$ is primitive in $Z$, and Gauss's lemma, equivalently the linear regime of [P6], makes $B$ absolutely irreducible. Hence it is squarefree.

Direct differentiation gives $B_Z=X$, and $\gcd(B,X)=1$ because $X\nmid H(Y)$. This also follows from [P1] since $D<dp$. For a degree-one polynomial, the normalized discriminant is $1$, whereas $\operatorname{Res}_Z(B,B_Z)=X$. Its zero set is the affine line $X=0$, which is smooth and absolutely irreducible.

For every $j$, one has $B(0,c_j,0)=0$ and $B_X(0,c_j,0)=0$, $B_Y(0,c_j,0)=H'(c_j)=0$, and $B_Z(0,c_j,0)=0$. The equality $H'(c_j)=0$ follows from the double factor $(Y-c_j)^2$, so every displayed lift is singular.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Let $p$ be prime and let $101\le d\le p-2$. Give $X,Y,Z$ weights $(1,1,d)$, and set $D=d+1$, $s=\lfloor(d+1)/2\rfloor$, and $e=d+1-2s\in\{0,1\}$. Choose distinct $c_1,\ldots,c_s\in\mathbb F_p$. If $e=1$, choose $b\in\mathbb F_p\setminus\{c_1,\ldots,c_s\}$, and define $H(Y)=\prod_{j=1}^s(Y-c_j)^2(Y-b)^e$ and $B(X,Y,Z)=XZ+H(Y)$, with the last factor omitted when $e=0$. Then $B$ is primitive in $Z$, squarefree, and absolutely irreducible, with $\operatorname{wdeg}B=D<p$, $B_Z=X$, and $\gcd(B,B_Z)=1$. Its normalized degree-one discriminant is $1$, while $\operatorname{Res}_Z(B,B_Z)=X$, whose zero set is a smooth absolutely irreducible affine line. For every $1\le j\le s$, the point $(0,c_j,0)$ is singular on $B=0$.
lemmas.title: Singular construction algebra

lemmas.proof_markdown:
For $m\ne0$, the factor $(Y-c_j)^2$ shows that $H(c_j+mt)$ is divisible by $t^2$; for $m=0$, it is identically zero. Hence each displayed quotient is a polynomial of degree at most $d$ and vanishes at $t=0$. Substitution gives $B(L_{j,m}(t),P_{j,m}(t))=t(-H(c_j+mt)/t)+H(c_j+mt)\equiv0$.

If $t\ne0$, the definition of $f$ gives $P_{j,m}(t)=f(t,c_j+mt)$. At $t=0$, both sides equal $0$. Thus every selected line is fully accepted. The selected base lines have equations $Y=c_j+mX$, so distinct pairs $(j,m)$ give distinct lines. Their number is $sp>D$, and their $sp^2$ accepted incidences have normalized mass $sp^2/[p^2(p+1)]=s/(p+1)$.

Finally, $B_Z(L_{j,m}(t),P_{j,m}(t))=t$, so exactly $t=0$ is ramified on each selected line. The $sp$ selected ramified incidences have normalized mass $sp/[p^2(p+1)]=s/[p(p+1)]$. The quotient defining $P_{j,m}$ is exact polynomial division; no value at $t=0$ is obtained by inversion.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Under the hypotheses and notation of [P7], for $1\le j\le s$ and $m\in\mathbb F_p$ define $L_{j,m}(t)=(t,c_j+mt)$ and $P_{j,m}(t)=-H(c_j+mt)/t$. Define $f:\mathbb F_p^2\to\mathbb F_p$ by $f(x,y)=-H(y)/x$ when $x\ne0$ and $f(0,y)=0$, and give every unselected affine line the constant label $0$. Then every $P_{j,m}$ is a polynomial of degree at most $d$ satisfying $B(L_{j,m}(t),P_{j,m}(t))\equiv0$, and every one of the $sp>D$ selected lines is fully accepted by $f$. Their uniform line measure is $s/(p+1)$, so the table's agreement is at least $s/(p+1)$. Moreover, $B_Z(L_{j,m}(t),P_{j,m}(t))=t$, so each selected line has exactly one ramified accepted parameter, and the normalized mass of the selected ramified incidences is $s/[p(p+1)]$.
lemmas.title: Explicit incidence table

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Suppose such a polynomial $Q$ existed. Then $R(X,Y)=XQ(X,Y)+H(Y)$ would have total degree at most $D=d+1$. For every selected line, $R(L_{j,m}(t))=B(L_{j,m}(t),Q(L_{j,m}(t)))=B(L_{j,m}(t),P_{j,m}(t))\equiv0$. Thus the defining linear polynomial of each of the $sp>D$ distinct selected lines would divide $R$. A nonzero polynomial of degree at most $D$ cannot have more than $D$ distinct affine-line factors, so $R=0$. This would imply $X\mid H(Y)$, a contradiction.

Now let $A$ be a graph interpolant of weighted degree at most $d$. Since $Z$ has weight $d$, it has the form $A(X,Y,Z)=aZ+b(X,Y)$, where $a\in\mathbb F_p$ and $\deg b\le d$. If $a=0$, then $b$ vanishes identically on more than $d$ distinct lines and hence $b=0$. If $a\ne0$, the polynomial $Q=-a^{-1}b$ has total degree at most $d$ and restricts to every selected label, contradicting the first part. Hence no nonzero interpolant has weighted degree at most $d$. Entry [P7] supplies the interpolant $B$ of weighted degree $D=d+1$, proving minimality.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Under the hypotheses and notation of [P8], there is no polynomial $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ such that $Q(L_{j,m}(t))\equiv P_{j,m}(t)$ for every $1\le j\le s$ and $m\in\mathbb F_p$. Moreover, every nonzero $A\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]$ satisfying $A(L_{j,m}(t),P_{j,m}(t))\equiv0$ for all selected lines has weighted degree at least $D=d+1$. Consequently, $B=XZ+H(Y)$ is a minimum-weight graph interpolant for the selected graph lines.
lemmas.title: Interpolation minimality

lemmas.proof_markdown:
The polynomial $A$ has degree $r=D-d$. Hence $\operatorname{wdeg}(Z^2)=2d$ and $\operatorname{wdeg}(AZ)=r+d=D$; since $2d\le D$, one has $\operatorname{wdeg}B_{\mathrm{sm}}=D$. As a degree-one polynomial in $Y$, $B_{\mathrm{sm}}$ is absolutely irreducible, and $(B_{\mathrm{sm}})_Y=1$ makes its hypersurface smooth. Since $p$ is odd, $(\Delta_{\mathrm{sm}})_Y=-4\ne0$. The discriminant is also degree one in $Y$, so it is smooth and absolutely irreducible.

On the displayed graph, $B_{\mathrm{sm}}(t,0,0)=0$, while $(B_{\mathrm{sm}})_Z(t,0,0)=A(t)=\prod_{i=1}^r(t-a_i)$. The $a_i$ are distinct, so this restriction has exactly $r=D-d$ roots. All corresponding lifts are smooth because $(B_{\mathrm{sm}})_Y=1$. This is consistent with [P5]: the roots occur at distinct base points, with only one displayed graph direction through each.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Let $p$ be prime, let $101\le d<p$, and let $2d\le D<p$. Give $X,Y,Z$ weights $(1,1,d)$, set $r=D-d$, choose distinct $a_1,\ldots,a_r\in\mathbb F_p$, and define $A(X)=\prod_{i=1}^r(X-a_i)$ and $B_{\mathrm{sm}}(X,Y,Z)=Z^2+A(X)Z+Y$. Then $B_{\mathrm{sm}}$ is monic in $Z$, has weighted degree $D$, and is smooth and absolutely irreducible. Its $Z$-discriminant $\Delta_{\mathrm{sm}}(X,Y)=A(X)^2-4Y$ is also smooth and absolutely irreducible. The label $P_L(t)=0$ on the line $L(t)=(t,0)$ satisfies $B_{\mathrm{sm}}(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0$, and $(B_{\mathrm{sm}})_Z(L(t),P_L(t))=A(t)$ has exactly $D-d$ distinct roots.
lemmas.title: Monic stress test

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Both terms of $B_{\mathrm{den}}$ have weighted degree $2d=D$. Over $\overline{\mathbb F}_p(X,Y)$, the element $XYg(X)^2$ is not a square because its valuation at $Y$ is odd. Since $p$ is odd, $Z^2-XYg(X)^2$ is irreducible over that field. Gauss's lemma makes $B_{\mathrm{den}}$ absolutely irreducible. It is squarefree and primitive, and [P1] applies because $D=2d<dp$.

For each nonzero square $s=c_s^2$, one has $P_s(t)^2=c_s^2t^2g(t)^2=st^2g(t)^2$, which equals $XYg(X)^2$ after substituting $(X,Y)=(t,st)$. Thus the graph identity holds, and the label has degree $d$. There are $(p-1)/2$ nonzero squares, while $(p-1)/2>2d=D$.

Since $(B_{\mathrm{den}})_Z=2Z$, its restriction to a graph is $2c_stg(t)$, whose distinct roots are $0,a_1,\ldots,a_{d-1}$. At each corresponding lift, $Z=0$, and either $X=Y=0$ or $g(X)=0$. The derivatives $(B_{\mathrm{den}})_X=-Yg^2-2XYgg'$, $(B_{\mathrm{den}})_Y=-Xg^2$, and $(B_{\mathrm{den}})_Z=2Z$ therefore all vanish, so every ramified lift is singular.

Finally, a polynomial root would satisfy $Q(X,Y)^2=XYg(X)^2$. The valuation at $Y$ is even on the left and equal to $1$ on the right, which is impossible.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Let $p$ be prime, let $d\ge101$, and assume $p>4d+1$. Give $X,Y,Z$ weights $(1,1,d)$, set $D=2d$, choose distinct nonzero $a_1,\ldots,a_{d-1}\in\mathbb F_p$, and define $g(X)=\prod_{i=1}^{d-1}(X-a_i)$ and $B_{\mathrm{den}}(X,Y,Z)=Z^2-XYg(X)^2$. Then $B_{\mathrm{den}}$ has weighted degree $D$ and is absolutely irreducible. For every nonzero square $s\in\mathbb F_p$, choose $c_s\in\mathbb F_p^\times$ with $c_s^2=s$ and set $L_s(t)=(t,st)$ and $P_s(t)=c_stg(t)$. Each $P_s$ has degree $d$ and satisfies $B_{\mathrm{den}}(L_s(t),P_s(t))\equiv0$. There are $(p-1)/2>D$ such graph lines. On every one, $(B_{\mathrm{den}})_Z$ vanishes at exactly the $d=D-d$ parameters $0,a_1,\ldots,a_{d-1}$, and every corresponding lift is singular on $B_{\mathrm{den}}=0$. There is no $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ satisfying $B_{\mathrm{den}}(X,Y,Q(X,Y))\equiv0$.
lemmas.title: Dense singular pencil

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Entries [P7]–[P9] give an absolutely irreducible interpolant of weight $D$ supporting $sp>D$ graph lines, but [P9] rules out a total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial restricting to all their labels; the equation $XQ+H=0$ also rules out a polynomial root. Entry [P11] supplies another absolutely irreducible example with more than $D$ graph directions and no polynomial root. These examples refute the first assertion.

For [P7] and [P8], $\operatorname{Res}_Z(B,B_Z)=X$ is a smooth absolutely irreducible line. Nevertheless, for each $j$, all $p$ lines indexed by $m\in\mathbb F_p$ pass through the same ramified lift $(0,c_j,0)$. This refutes the second assertion.

In [P10], the interpolant is monic and both its hypersurface and its discriminant are smooth and absolutely irreducible, while the displayed graph line contains exactly $D-d$ ramified parameters. This is not $o(D-d)$ and refutes the third assertion.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let $p$ be prime, let $101\le d<p$, and give $X,Y,Z$ weights $(1,1,d)$. The following assertions hold:

1. If an absolutely irreducible graph interpolant of weighted degree at most $D<p$ supports more than $D$ distinct affine graph lines with degree-at-most-$d$ labels, then it has a polynomial root $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ satisfying $B(X,Y,Q(X,Y))\equiv0$, without any simple-common-lift hypothesis.

2. Smooth absolute irreducibility of the raw-resultant curve $\operatorname{Res}_Z(B,B_Z)=0$ controls the number of graph directions meeting a ramified lifted point.

3. If $2d\le D<p$, a graph interpolant is monic in $Z$, and its $Z$-discriminant is smooth and absolutely irreducible, then every degree-at-most-$d$ graph line contains $o(D-d)$ parameters at which $B_Z$ vanishes.
lemmas.title: Simplicity substitutes

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Applying [P3] to the geometrically reducible factors of weights $\delta_i$ and summing gives at most $\sum_i\delta_i^2/(4d)\le D^2/(4d)$ removed graph lines. After uniform-incidence normalization, their cost is at most $D^2/[4dp(p+1)]=O(1/(\epsilon p))$ under the stated envelope. Entry [P5] bounds the smooth ramified incidences for a fixed assigned factor by $p^2$, hence by normalized mass $1/(p+1)$. These estimates require the stated factor assignment and lifted-point smoothness; [P12] shows that absolute irreducibility alone does not supply the latter.

If the remaining singular incidences are deleted using the per-line budget, their normalized cost is $O(D/p)=O(\sqrt{d/(\epsilon p)})$. Requiring this quantity to be $O(\epsilon)$ gives $\sqrt{d/(\epsilon p)}=O(\epsilon)$, which is equivalent, up to absolute constants, to $\epsilon^3=\Omega(d/p)$. The calculation is conditional on this deletion architecture and does not give a lower bound for methods that globally control singular accepted lifts.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Let $p$ be prime, let $101\le d<p$, and let $0<\epsilon\le1$. Suppose the interpolation weight satisfies $D=O(\sqrt{dp/\epsilon})$. Suppose a deletion argument assigns supported graph lines to fixed $\mathbb F_p$-irreducible factors, deletes graph lines supported on geometrically reducible factors using [P3], applies [P5] only to ramified lifts known to be smooth on their assigned factor, and charges every remaining singular ramified incidence by the per-line budget $D/p$. Then the normalized purification loss is $O(1/(\epsilon p))$, the normalized smooth-ramification loss for each fixed assigned factor is at most $1/(p+1)$, and the singular-ramification loss is $O(D/p)=O(\sqrt{d/(\epsilon p)})$. Requiring the last loss to be $O(\epsilon)$ imposes $\epsilon^3=\Omega(d/p)$.
lemmas.title: Singular deletion scale
